SoundGuys reports attenuation in decibels at particular frequencies. Noise cancelling works best on steady low-pitched sound: engine hum, air conditioning, the drone of a flight. As a rule of thumb, a reduction of 10 dB is heard as roughly half as loud, so the gap between a pair that cuts 10 to 20 dB and one that cuts more than 25 dB is the gap between a quieter commute and one where the hum nearly disappears. Nothing at this price silences a crying baby or a nearby conversation, because those sit at higher frequencies where ANC is weakest. The trade-off is the noise cancelling itself: SoundGuys measured 10 to 20 dB of cancellation under 700 Hz, the weakest of the four. That is enough to take the edge off a bus or an open office, and not enough to feel like a different room on a plane. SoundGuys measured 42 hours 57 minutes of battery with noise cancelling on. The LDAC advantage is real only if your phone and your music source support it; on an iPhone, which does not use LDAC, you would be paying for a feature you cannot use.
